mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain certified copy from New Zealand Companies Office. If the destination jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention: submit the certified copy to the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit for an Apostille certificate; no consular step. If the destination jurisdiction is not a member: submit the certified copy to the Department of Internal Affairs for authentication, then present it to the consular section of the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive routes; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request official Certificate of Good Standing from New Zealand Companies Office. For Hague Apostille member states: obtain Apostille certificate from New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit; no consular certification. For non-member states: obtain Department of Internal Affairs authentication certificate and then consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in Wellington. Do not apply both an Apostille and consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial directors and shareholders of the proposed New Zealand company, executed before a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the Board Resolution and Power of Attorney before a New Zealand notary public; the notary certifies the signatures and capacity. If the destination state is a Hague Apostille member: the notarial certificate is authenticated by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs with an Apostille, and no consular step follows. If the destination state is non-member: the notarial certificate is authenticated by the Department of Internal Affairs and then legalized by the destination state's consulate in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subscriber shareholders adopting the constitution, with certification by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Adopt the Articles of Association by unanimous shareholder resolution; have a certified notarial copy prepared by a New Zealand notary. For Hague Apostille states: attach a Department of Internal Affairs Apostille to the notarial certificate; no consular action. For non-Hague states: obtain Department of Internal Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank at which the beneficial owner, director, or intended shareholder maintains an active account; if the bank is in New Zealand, the issuing bank is the entity, otherwise the issuing bank is the institution in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the bank's authorized officer sign the reference letter. If the issuing bank is in New Zealand: notarize the bank officer's signature, then for Hague Apostille states apply to the Department of Internal Affairs for an Apostille; for non-Hague states apply to the Department of Internal Affairs for authentication and then consular legalization at the destination state's consulate in New Zealand. If the issuing bank is outside New Zealand, the document must be authenticated in the bank's own country under that country's Apostille or consular legalization system; a New Zealand Apostille must never be added to a foreign document. Apostille and consular legalization remain parallel and exclusive paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding or incorporation, the full UBO chain and all directors, shareholders, senior managers, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand Financial Sanctions Register and Designated Persons List maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit's warning and guidance on suspicious transactions, the OFAC SDN List and all relevant OFAC sanctions programs, and global PEP databases such as World-Check, Refinitiv, or Acuris. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any domestic or foreign PEP, family member, or close associate, and a negative news search and source-of-wealth review must be documented. Sanctions screening must be repeated within 24 hours before any distribution, dividend, payment, or transaction involving payout rails such as Stripe and PayPal, and no funds may be released to or from New Zealand if any sanctions or PEP red flag exists unless the regulator or MFAT provides explicit authorization.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office via the New Zealand Companies Register and NZBN Name Reservation Portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may use Latin script letters, Arabic numerals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, ampersands, full stops, commas, and parentheses; Māori macrons are accepted. Chinese characters and other non-Latin scripts are not accepted, so any Chinese or foreign trade name must be rendered in romanized or pinyin transliteration. The Companies Office applies a four-tier screening doctrine: Tier 1 exact match against existing company names and reserved names; Tier 2 almost-identical phonetic, typographic, and semantic variants; Tier 3 prohibited and sensitive tokens requiring ministerial or regulator consent; Tier 4 reserved-name conflict and common-law passing-off risk. For a limited liability company, the legal name must end with 'Limited' or 'Tapui Limited' unless an exemption is obtained under the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may within 20 working days submit a written reconsideration request to the New Zealand Companies Office stating the proposed name, the rejection reference number, the factual and legal grounds for reversal, and any supporting evidence. If the rejection is based on similarity, submit a written consent letter from the registered holder of the conflicting name or evidence of prior continuous use. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, obtain the appropriate ministerial or regulatory approval and resubmit. A granted name reservation is valid for 20 working days and cannot be extended; the applicant must reapply after expiry. If the Companies Office maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not absolutely prohibited as a New Zealand registered office address under section 190 of the Companies Act 1993, provided the address is a physical street address in New Zealand at which documents may be served during normal business hours. However, for an e-commerce entity in ISIC 4791 selling baby and maternity supplies online, Inland Revenue and major New Zealand trading banks will likely reject a pure virtual mailbox as the sole business address for GST registration, corporate bank account opening, and AML/CFT verification because it fails to demonstrate genuine commercial substance. A serviced office with a physical reception, named agent, and document-forwarding service is preferable. Stripe and PayPal underwriting will also require a physical operating address and a bank account matching the legal entity. For the International Company tax-exempt structure, the availability of a nominated agent in New Zealand or an associated jurisdiction is critical to satisfy the Companies Office and any payment processor.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: physical signage at the registered office; a person or agent available to accept service during business hours; accounting records, statutory registers, and AML/CFT records maintained at or accessible from the registered office; no PO Box used as the registered office; a clearly identifiable fulfilment or storage address if physical inventory is claimed; and consistency between the GST address, bank address, and merchant processor address. Quantified risk: Low but non-zero, estimated at approximately 10-15% annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice compliance visit by Inland Revenue, the Companies Office, or a local council in response to a complaint or GST anomaly; an online-only business with no physical stock and no complaints faces a lower likelihood of field audit.
